question: The SI unit of temperature is/are _____
solution:
The correct answer is __kelvin.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Kelvin__ is the SI unit of temperature.
 
• It is one of the seven base units in the International System of Units (SI).
 
• The kelvin is defined based on the Boltzmann constant, which relates the average kinetic energy of particles in a substance to its temperature.
 
• The symbol for kelvin is K.
 
• Unlike Celsius and Fahrenheit, kelvin does not use the term "degree" and does not include a degree symbol.
 
• 0 K (zero kelvin) represents absolute zero, the theoretical point where all molecular motion ceases.
 
• Kelvin is widely used in scientific contexts, especially in physics and chemistry, for precise temperature measurements.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Celsius:**

 
 
• Celsius is a temperature scale where the freezing point of water is 0°C and the boiling point is 100°C under standard atmospheric conditions.
 
• It is commonly used in daily life and non-scientific contexts.
 
 
 
• **Fahrenheit: **
 
 
• The Fahrenheit scale is primarily used in the United States.
 
• In this scale, water freezes at 32°F and boils at 212°F under standard atmospheric conditions.
 
 
 
• **Absolute Zero:**
 
 
• Absolute zero is the lowest possible temperature, equivalent to 0 K or -273.15°C.
 
• At this point, molecular motion theoretically stops.
